messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
messages.body_plain:
On Sun, 2012-04-01 at 00:46 -0700, Chris wrote:
> Hi all,
> I've been trying for a week to work around this error.
>
>
> #####
> file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 64e669042e54  date: Fri Mar 16 12:57:24 2012
> +0100
> Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 780, Thread:
> 0
> Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

When we get 'Fail to factorize Q' it means that the precision matrix is
numerically singular. In most cases it is not, but it can still be so
numerically for some ''almost ill-defined models''.

When the precision matrix *is* singular, this is usually due to the
improper default prior for the intercept, so setting
control.fixed=list(prec.intecept=0.001), or similar, will solve the
issue.

the intrinsic models, are almost singular, as they have a constr=TRUE
default, which ensure they are not. However, numerically, they are
computed without the constraint and then we correct for the constraint.
this means there are some small epsilons around to make non-sinuglar.
This the argument 'diagonal=' in the 'f()', which is default 1e-6 for
intrinsic models. This constant can be to small in some cases.

so, increasing the diagonal argument and setting a proper prior for the
intercept, solves the issue.

set.seed (1)
n <- 500
t <- 25 ## n observations per loc
y <- rnorm(n*t)
x <- y+rnorm(n*t)
t2 <- rep(1:t,each=n)
id <- rep(1:n,each=t)

data <- data.frame("y"=y, "x"=x, "t2"=t2, "id"=id)
A = matrix(runif(n^2), n, n)
B <-inla.matrix2graph(A) # tried as a grap

diag.eps = 1e-4
test <- inla(y~x+f(id, model="besag", graph=B, diagonal=diag.eps)+
             f(t2, model="rw2", diagonal = diag.eps),
             data=data, family="gaussian",
             verbose=T,
             control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.01))

rho = 0.9 ## sparse matrix example
Q = toeplitz(c(1+rho^2, -rho,  rep(0, n-3), -rho)) / (1-rho^2)
Q = inla.as.dgTMatrix(Q)

diag.eps = 1e-3
test2 <- inla(y~x+f(id, model="besag", graph=Q,  diagonal=diag.eps) +
              f(t2, model="rw2", diagonal=diag.eps),
              data=data, family="gaussian",
              verbose=TRUE,
              keep=TRUE,
              control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.01))

--
INLA help <he...@r-inla.org>
R-INLA

messages.subject: Connected components in BYM models
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to estimate besag models for administrative regional data in Columbia (http://www.worldofmaps.net/en/south-america/map-colombia/map-provinces-colombia.htm).  My graph file looks correct, but I get warnings about the number of connected components (INLA reads 6 different cc's) and the model undergoing revisions accordingly.  Do you mind giving a text-book definition of a cc in this context.  I'm worried my graphing file may be incorrect, b/c single area cc's are noted for not only the islands of San Andres and Providencia (no surprise there) but also for Atlantico, Guajira, and Quindio (I guess I don't fully understand why these would be cc's on there own).

Thank you.

messages.subject: Placing random effects vector inside inla.make.lincombs() function
messages.subject_clean: Placing random effects vector inside inla.make.lincombs() function
messages.body_plain:
Having trouble estimating a linear combination of effects using the lincombs() function.  Would like to estimate a linear combination of some but not all random effects and fixed effects, but it appears that the only random effect included in all linear combinations is the first.  The lincomb() function appears to work fine, and I can use it as a work-around by concatenating one of these for each required random effect (example below).

This seems to be true even for a simple adaptation of the lincomb() FAQ example:

## A simple model
n = 100
a = rnorm(n)
b = rnorm(n)
idx = 1:n
y = rnorm(n) + a + b
formula = y ~ 1 + a + b + f(idx, model="iid")

lc1 = inla.make.lincomb(idx = c(1,NA,rep(NA,n-2))) #estimate random effect for 1st level of idx
lc2 = inla.make.lincomb(idx = c(NA,1,rep(NA,n-2))) #estimate random effect for 2nd level of idx
all.lc <http://all.lc> = c(lc1,lc2)
names(all.lc <http://all.lc>) <- c("lc1","lc2")
lc3 = inla.make.lincombs(idx = c(1,1,rep(NA,n-2))) #estimate random effects of 1st & 2nd levels of idx

r1 = inla(formula, data = data.frame(a,b,y),lincomb = all.lc <http://all.lc>,control.data = list(initial=10, fixed=TRUE),
control.inla= list(lincomb.derived.only=TRUE,verbose=T))

r1$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[1] == r1$summary.random$idx$mean[1] #evaluates to TRUE
r1$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[2] == r1$summary.random$idx$mean[2] #evaluates to TRUE

r2 = inla(formula, data = data.frame(a,b,y),lincomb = lc3,control.data = list(initial=10, fixed=TRUE),
control.inla = list(lincomb.derived.only=TRUE))

r2$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[1] == r2$summary.random$idx$mean[1] #evaluates to TRUE
r2$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[2] == r2$summary.random$idx$mean[2] #evaluates to FALSE because the left-hand side of the equality just repeats the random effect for the 1st idx level
I'm sure I'm missing some subtlety of the lincombs() specification.  Can you help?  Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Placing random effects vector inside inla.make.lincombs() function
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] Placing random effects vector inside inla.make.lincombs() function
messages.body_plain:
On Sat, 2012-04-14 at 20:46 -0700, David wrote:
> Having trouble estimating a linear combination of effects using the
> lincombs() function.  Would like to estimate a linear combination of
> some but not all random effects and fixed effects, but it appears that
> the only random effect included in all linear combinations is the
> first.  The lincomb() function appears to work fine, and I can use it
> as a work-around by concatenating one of these for each required
> random effect (example below).

as model 'idx' has length > 1 or a f()-model, then its entry in
make.lincomb is a vector and a matrix in make.lincomb*s*. That is the
error.

the notion is that

	inla.make.lincombs(idx = A)

where A is a matrix, is the same as the union of

	inla.make.lincomb(idx = A[1,])

and so, for all the rows. so each *row* of A spesify on linear
combination.

I attach an updated and corrected example, hope this helps.

--

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] error when applying inla on a grid dataset
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] error when applying inla on a grid dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeff,
Assuming the right things are in india.struct (the ith component
should be the region that observation i is in), then your call appears
to be correct.

Can you send the graph file?  There's a decent chance that there's
something wrong in that (that's the most common problem).  You could
try to run inla.debug.graph(graph.file) on it and it may tell you
what's wrong.

Can you also check that you're using the newest version of INLA (run
inla.update(testing=TRUE))

Best,

Dan
